children.translated_text: Now, therefore, we shall explain <s>dharma</s>. | KVs 1.1.1 |
That from which the attainment of prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>) and the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>) results—that is <s>dharma</s>. | KVs 1.1.2 |
The authority of the Veda (<s>āmnāya</s>) is due to its being the word of that [<s>dharma</s>]. | KVs 1.1.3 |

children.text: dharmaviśeṣa prasūtāt dravyaguṇakarmasāmānya viśeṣasamavāyānāṃ padārthānāṃ sādharmyavaidharmyābhyāṃ tattvajñānānniḥśreyasam | KVs_1,1.4 |
children.translated_text: The highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>) results from the knowledge of the reality of the categories (<s>padārtha</s>)—substance (<s>dravya</s>), quality (<s>guṇa</s>), action (<s>karma</s>), universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), particularity (<s>viśeṣa</s>), and inherence (<s>samavāya</s>)—through their similarities and differences, produced from a particular <s>dharma</s>. | KVs 1.1.4 |

children.text: pṛthivyāpastejo vāyurākāśaṃ kālo digātmā mana iti dravyāṇi | KVs_1,1.5 |
children.translated_text: Earth, water, fire, air, space (<s>ākāśa</s>), time, direction, self (<s>ātman</s>), and mind (<s>manas</s>)—these are the substances (<s>dravya</s>). | KVs 1.1.5 |

children.text: ruparasagandhasparśāḥ saṃkhyāḥ parimāṇāni pṛthaktvaṃ saṃyogavibhāgau paratvāparatve buddhayaḥ sukhaduḥkhe icchādveṣau prayatnāśca guṇāḥ | KVs_1,1.6 |
children.translated_text: Color, taste, smell, touch, numbers, measures, separateness, conjunction and disjunction, priority and posteriority, cognitions, pleasure and pain, desire and aversion, and effort—these are the qualities (<s>guṇa</s>). | KVs 1.1.6 |

children.text: utkṣepaṇamavakṣepaṇaṃ ākuñcanaṃ prasāraṇaṃ gamanamiti karmāṇi | KVs_1,1.7 |
children.translated_text: Throwing upward, throwing downward, contraction, expansion, and locomotion—these are the actions (<s>karma</s>). | KVs 1.1.7 |

children.text: sadanityaṃ dravyavat kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ sāmānyaviśeṣavaditi dravyaguṇakarmaṇāmaviśeṣaḥ | KVs_1,1.8 |
children.translated_text: Being existent, non-eternal, having substance as substratum, being an effect and a cause, and possessing universals and particulars—this is what is common among substance, quality, and action. | KVs 1.1.8 |
The similarity between substance and quality is that both produce effects of the same class (<s>sajātīya</s>). | KVs 1.1.9 |
Substances produce other substances, and qualities produce other qualities. | KVs 1.1.10 |
An action producible by action does not exist. | KVs 1.1.11 |

children.text: na dravyaṃ kāraṇaṃ ca bhavati | KVs_1,1.12 |
children.translated_text: [Action] is neither a substance nor a cause. | KVs 1.1.12 |
Qualities are of both kinds [i.e., both effects and causes]. | KVs 1.1.13 |
Action is opposed to the effect [it produces, i.e., it destroys the conjunction that caused the substance]. | KVs 1.1.14 |
That which possesses action and quality and is an inherent cause (<s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>)—this is the definition of substance. | KVs 1.1.15 |

Having substance as substratum, possessing no [further] qualities, not an [independent] cause of conjunction and disjunction, and not dependent [on other qualities]—this is the definition of quality. | KVs 1.1.16 |
Residing in one substance, devoid of quality, an independent cause of conjunction and disjunction—this is the definition of action. | KVs 1.1.17 |
Substance is the common cause of substance, quality, and action. | KVs 1.1.18 |
Likewise, quality [is also a common cause]. | KVs 1.1.19 |
Action is the common [cause] of conjunction, disjunction, and velocity. | KVs 1.1.20 |
[Action is] not [a common cause] of substances. | KVs 1.1.21 |
Because of [its] difference [from substances]. | KVs 1.1.22 |
Substance is the common effect of substances. | KVs 1.1.23 |
Because of dissimilarity from quality, action is not [the effect] of actions. | KVs 1.1.24 |

children.text: dvitvaprabhṛtayaḥ saṃkhyāḥ pṛthaktva saṃyoga vibhāgāśca | KVs_1,1.25 |
children.translated_text: Numbers beginning from two, separateness, conjunction, and disjunction [are produced in many substances simultaneously]. | KVs 1.1.25 |

children.text: asamavāyāt sāmānyakāryaṃ karma na vidyate | KVs_1,1.26 |
children.translated_text: Because of non-inherence, a common effect of action does not exist. | KVs 1.1.26 |
Substance is [the common cause] of conjunctions. | KVs 1.1.27 |
Color [of the effect is produced] from the colors [of the causes]. | KVs 1.1.28 |
Throwing upward [results from] heaviness (<s>gurutva</s>), effort (<s>prayatna</s>), and conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>). | KVs 1.1.29 |
And conjunction and disjunction [result] from actions. | KVs 1.1.30 |
In the generality of causation, it has been stated that action is not a cause of substances and actions. | KVs 1.1.31 |
From the absence of the cause, the absence of the effect follows. | KVs 1.2.1 |
But from the absence of the effect, the absence of the cause does not follow. | KVs 1.2.2 |
'Universal and particular' is relative to cognition. | KVs 1.2.3 |
Being (<s>bhāva</s>) is indeed a universal alone, because it is the cause of continued recognition. | KVs 1.2.4 |

children.text: dravyatvaṃ guṇatvaṃ karmatvaṃ ca sāmānyāni viśeṣāśca | KVs_1,2.5 |
children.translated_text: Substance-ness (<s>dravyatva</s>), quality-ness (<s>guṇatva</s>), and action-ness (<s>karmatva</s>) are both universals and particulars. | KVs 1.2.5 |
Except for the ultimate particulars (<s>antyaviśeṣa</s>). | KVs 1.2.6 |

children.text: saditi yato dravyaguṇakarmasu sā sattā | KVs_1,2.7 |
children.translated_text: That by which the designation 'existent' applies to substance, quality, and action—that is existence (<s>sattā</s>). | KVs 1.2.7 |
Existence (<s>sattā</s>) is a thing different from substance, quality, and action. | KVs 1.2.8 |

children.text: guṇakarmasu ca bhāvānna karma na guṇaḥ | KVs_1,2.9 |
children.translated_text: And being present in qualities and actions, [existence] is neither an action nor a quality. | KVs 1.2.9 |
And because of the absence of [further] universals and particulars [belonging to it]. | KVs 1.2.10 |
Substance-ness is stated [as a universal] because of its presence in many substances. | KVs 1.2.11 |
And because of the absence of universals and particulars [within it]. | KVs 1.2.12 |
Likewise, quality-ness is stated because of its being in qualities. | KVs 1.2.13 |
And because of the absence of universals and particulars. | KVs 1.2.14 |
Action-ness is stated because of its being in actions. | KVs 1.2.15 |
And because of the absence of universals and particulars. | KVs 1.2.16 |
Because the mark 'existent' is without distinction, and because of the absence of a distinguishing mark, existence (<s>bhāva</s>) is one. | KVs 1.2.17 |
Earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>) possesses color, taste, smell, and touch. | KVs 2.1.1 |
Waters (<s>āpas</s>) possess color, taste, and touch; they are fluid and viscous. | KVs 2.1.2 |
Fire (<s>tejas</s>) possesses color and touch. | KVs 2.1.3 |
Air (<s>vāyu</s>) possesses touch. | KVs 2.1.4 |
These [qualities] do not exist in space (<s>ākāśa</s>). | KVs 2.1.5 |
The fluidity of ghee, lac, and beeswax produced from contact with fire is a similarity with water. | KVs 2.1.6 |

children.text: trapusīsa loha rajata suvarṇānāmagnisaṃyogāddravatvamadbhiḥ sāmānyam | KVs_2,1.7 |
children.translated_text: The fluidity of tin, lead, iron, silver, and gold produced from contact with fire is a similarity with water. | KVs 2.1.7 |

children.text: viṣāṇī kakudmān prāntevāladhiḥ sāsnāvān iti gotve dṛṣṭaṃ liṅgam | KVs_2,1.8 |
children.translated_text: Having horns, having a hump, having a tail with hair at the end, and having a dewlap—this is the observed mark of cow-ness (<s>gotva</s>). | KVs 2.1.8 |
And touch is [the mark] of air. | KVs 2.1.9 |

children.text: na ca dṛṣṭānāṃ sparśa ityadṛṣṭaliṅgo vāyuḥ | KVs_2,1.10 |
children.translated_text: And since the touch is not of visible [substances], air is that whose mark is imperceptible. | KVs 2.1.10 |
[Air] is a substance because it does not inhere in [another] substance. | KVs 2.1.11 |
Because it possesses action and qualities. | KVs 2.1.12 |
Eternity [of air] is stated because of not being a [composite] substance. | KVs 2.1.13 |
The aggregation of air with air is a mark of its plurality. | KVs 2.1.14 |

children.text: vāyusannikarṣe pratyakṣābhāvāt dṛṣṭaṃ liṅgaṃ na vidyate | KVs_2,1.15 |
children.translated_text: Since there is no perceptual cognition from contact with air, there is no observed mark [for air]. | KVs 2.1.15 |
And there is no distinction from what is generally observed. | KVs 2.1.16 |
Therefore, [the knowledge of air] is scriptural (<s>āgamika</s>). | KVs 2.1.17 |
The act of naming is a mark of [beings] superior to us. | KVs 2.1.18 |
Because the act of naming proceeds from perception. | KVs 2.1.19 |
Going out and entering in are the marks of space (<s>ākāśa</s>). | KVs 2.1.20 |
That is not a [valid] mark [of space], because action resides in one substance only. | KVs 2.1.21 |
And because of dissimilarity from the conformity to another cause. | KVs 2.1.22 |
From conjunction, there is cessation of action. | KVs 2.1.23 |
The quality of the effect is observed to be preceded by the quality of the cause. | KVs 2.1.24 |
And because of the non-manifestation of another effect, sound is not a quality of things possessing touch. | KVs 2.1.25 |

children.text: paratra samavāyāt pratyakṣatvācca nātmaguṇo na manoguṇaḥ | KVs_2,1.26 |
children.translated_text: Because of inherence in something external, and because of perceptibility, [sound] is neither a quality of the self nor of the mind. | KVs 2.1.26 |
By the method of elimination, [sound] is the mark of space (<s>ākāśa</s>). | KVs 2.1.27 |
Substance-ness and eternity [of space] are explained by analogy with air. | KVs 2.1.28 |
Because of the existence of that inherent nature. | KVs 2.1.29 |
And because there is no distinction in the mark of sound, and because of the absence of a distinguishing mark— | KVs 2.1.30 |
[Space is] one and distinct, because of conformity to that [sound]. | KVs 2.1.31 |

children.text: puṣpavastrayoḥ sati sannikarṣe guṇāntarāprādurbhāvo vastre gandhābhāvaliṅgam | KVs_2,2.1 |
children.translated_text: When a flower and a cloth are in contact, the non-production of a different quality in the cloth is the mark of the absence of smell in cloth. | KVs 2.2.1 |
Smell is established exclusively in earth. | KVs 2.2.2 |
By this, heat is explained. | KVs 2.2.3 |
Heat belongs to fire. | KVs 2.2.4 |
Coldness belongs to water. | KVs 2.2.5 |

children.text: aparasminnaparaṃ yugapat ciraṃ kṣipramiti kālaliṅgāni | KVs_2,2.6 |
children.translated_text: 'Later than another,' 'simultaneously,' 'for a long duration,' 'quickly'—these are the marks of time (<s>kāla</s>). | KVs 2.2.6 |
Substance-ness and eternity [of time] are explained by analogy with air. | KVs 2.2.7 |
Because of the existence of that inherent nature. | KVs 2.2.8 |
Because of its absence in eternal [substances] and presence in non-eternal [substances], in the cause it is designated as time. | KVs 2.2.9 |
'From here, this'—that from which [such usage arises] is the mark of direction (<s>diś</s>). | KVs 2.2.10 |
Substance-ness and eternity [of direction] are explained by analogy with air. | KVs 2.2.11 |
Because of the existence of that inherent nature. | KVs 2.2.12 |
The plurality [of directions] is established by the particularity of effects. | KVs 2.2.13 |

children.text: ādityasaṃyogāt bhūtapūrvāt bhaviṣyato bhūtācca prācī | KVs_2,2.14 |
children.translated_text: The east is established from the conjunction with the sun—past, future, and present. | KVs 2.2.14 |

children.text: tathā dakṣiṇā pratīcī udīcī ca | KVs_2,2.15 |
children.translated_text: Similarly, the south, west, and north. | KVs 2.2.15 |
By this, the intermediate directions are explained. | KVs 2.2.16 |
Doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>) arises from the perception of a common feature and the recollection of a specific feature. | KVs 2.2.17 |
And what is seen may be doubted as something previously seen. | KVs 2.2.18 |
And because of appearing as seen before and not as seen before. | KVs 2.2.19 |
And doubt arises from knowledge and ignorance. | KVs 2.2.20 |
That object which is grasped by the ear is sound (<s>śabda</s>). | KVs 2.2.21 |
Because a particular feature is seen in both ways among things of the same class that are different. | KVs 2.2.22 |
[Sound] is not a substance, because it inheres in a single substance. | KVs 2.2.23 |
Nor is it an action, because it is not visible. | KVs 2.2.24 |
The cessation of a quality that exists—this is the similarity of [sound] with actions. | KVs 2.2.25 |
Because of the absence of a mark of [sound] being eternal. | KVs 2.2.26 |
Because of dissimilarity from eternal entities. | KVs 2.2.27 |
And this [sound] is non-eternal, because it has a cause. | KVs 2.2.28 |
And this is not established [as eternal] from [the theory of] modification. | KVs 2.2.29 |
Because of the defect in [the theory of] manifestation (<s>abhivyakti</s>). | KVs 2.2.30 |
The production of sound results from conjunction, from disjunction, and from another sound. | KVs 2.2.31 |
And from the mark [of being produced], sound is non-eternal. | KVs 2.2.32 |
But because of the absence of the two activities [conjunction and disjunction in space, sound's non-production cannot be established thus]. | KVs 2.2.33 |
Because the first [sound is produced] without a preceding sound. | KVs 2.2.34 |
And because of the occurrence of apprehension [only after production]. | KVs 2.2.35 |
[These reasons] are doubtful when there is multiplicity. | KVs 2.2.36 |
The absence of number is established generally. | KVs 2.2.37 |
The objects of the senses are well-established. | KVs 3.1.1 |
The non-establishment of sense-objects is the reason for [inferring] a thing different from the sense-objects. | KVs 3.1.2 |
That [inference] is fallacious (<s>anapadeśa</s>). | KVs 3.1.3 |
Because of ignorance of the cause. | KVs 3.1.4 |
Because of knowledge in [some] effects. | KVs 3.1.5 |
And because of ignorance [in other cases]. | KVs 3.1.6 |
'The cause is altogether different'—this is a fallacious inference. | KVs 3.1.7 |
For one thing is not the ground of proof (<s>apadeśa</s>) for another [unrelated] thing. | KVs 3.1.8 |

What is conjoined (<s>saṃyogin</s>), what inheres in the same (<s>samavāyin</s>), what co-inheres in the same substrate (<s>ekārthasamavāyin</s>), and what is opposed (<s>virodhin</s>) — | KVs 3.1.9 |
An effect [is the ground of proof] for another effect. | KVs 3.1.10 |
What is opposed and non-existent [is the ground of proof] for the existent. | KVs 3.1.11 |
The existent [is the ground of proof] for the non-existent. | KVs 3.1.12 |
The existent [is the ground of proof] for [another] existent. | KVs 3.1.13 |
Because a ground of proof presupposes [something] well-established. | KVs 3.1.14 |
What is not well-established is not a ground of proof; and what is non-existent or doubtful is not a ground of proof. | KVs 3.1.15 |
'Because it has horns, therefore it is a horse' — | KVs 3.1.16 |
'Because it has horns, therefore it is a cow' — this is an example of the inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). | KVs 3.1.17 |
That which is produced from the contact of self, sense-faculty, and object is one thing [i.e., perception]; the other is [inference]. | KVs 3.1.18 |

children.text: pravṛttinivṛttī ca pratyagātmani dṛṣṭe paratra liṅgam | KVs_3,1.19 |
children.translated_text: Activity and cessation, seen in the inner self (<s>pratyagātman</s>), are the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) [for their existence] in others. | KVs 3.1.19 |
The arising and non-arising of cognition from the contact of self, sense-faculty, and object is the inferential mark of the mind (<s>manas</s>). | KVs 3.2.1 |

children.text: tasya dravyatva nityatve vāyunā vyākhyāte | KVs_3,2.2 |
children.translated_text: Its substantiality (<s>dravyatva</s>) and eternality (<s>nityatva</s>) have been explained by [the analogy with] air (<s>vāyu</s>). | KVs 3.2.2 |
From the non-simultaneity of effort and the non-simultaneity of cognition, [the mind] is one [in each body]. | KVs 3.2.3 |

Inhalation (<s>prāṇa</s>), exhalation (<s>apāna</s>), closing and opening of the eyes, life, mental movement, the transformations of the other sense-faculties, pleasure, pain, desire, aversion, and effort — these are the marks (<s>liṅga</s>) of the self (<s>ātman</s>). | KVs 3.2.4 |
Its substantiality and eternality have been explained by [the analogy with] air. | KVs 3.2.5 |

children.text: yajñadatta iti sannikarṣe pratyakṣābhāvāt dṛṣṭaṃ liṅgaṃ na vidyate | KVs_3,2.6 |
children.translated_text: Since there is no perception in the [mere] contact [named] '<s>Yajñadatta</s>,' there is no observed inferential mark. | KVs 3.2.6 |
And from the generally observed [inference], there is no distinction [between selves]. | KVs 3.2.7 |
Therefore, [the knowledge of the self's identity] is scriptural (<s>āgamika</s>). | KVs 3.2.8 |
From the distinctness of the word 'I,' [the knowledge of self-identity] is not [merely] scriptural. | KVs 3.2.9 |

children.text: yadi dṛṣṭamanvakṣamahaṃ devadatto 'haṃ yajñadatta iti | KVs_3,2.10 |
children.translated_text: If [the knowledge] were observed, [one could say] 'I am <s>Devadatta</s>' [and] 'I am <s>Yajñadatta</s>.' | KVs 3.2.10 |

children.text: dṛṣṭyātmani liṅge eka eva dṛḍhatvāt pratyakṣavat pratyayaḥ | KVs_3,2.11 |
children.translated_text: When the inferential mark is seen in the self, the cognition is like perception, being firm in a single [self]. | KVs 3.2.11 |

children.text: devadatto gacchati yajñadatto gacchatītyupacārāccharīre pratyayaḥ | KVs_3,2.12 |
children.translated_text: '<s>Devadatta</s> goes,' '<s>Yajñadatta</s> goes' — the cognition regarding the body is through figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>). | KVs 3.2.12 |
But figurative usages are doubtful. | KVs 3.2.13 |

children.text: ahamiti pratyagātmani bhāvāt paratrābhāvādarthāntara pratyakṣaḥ | KVs_3,2.14 |
children.translated_text: Because of the presence [of the cognition] 'I' in the inner self and its absence elsewhere, [the self is known] through perception as a distinct entity. | KVs 3.2.14 |

'<s>Devadatta</s> goes' — from figurative usage and from identification [with the body], the ego-sense (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>) is [mistakenly treated as] a perception of that [extent of the] body. | KVs 3.2.15 |
But the figurative usage is doubtful. | KVs 3.2.16 |
Not through the distinction of body is the self an object of knowledge for <s>Yajñadatta</s> and <s>Viṣṇumitra</s>. | KVs 3.2.17 |

Since the distinction [of the self] is established from the primary and the applicable [senses of] 'I,' and from the non-deviation of the distinction — like a word — [the knowledge of self] is not [merely] scriptural. | KVs 3.2.18 |
From the non-distinction in the production of pleasure, pain, and cognition, [some argue for] the unity of self. | KVs 3.2.19 |
From [the evidence of] orderly arrangement, [the selves are] many. | KVs 3.2.20 |
And from the authority of scripture. | KVs 3.2.21 |
What exists and has no cause is eternal. | KVs 4.1.1 |
Its effect is the inferential mark [of its existence]. | KVs 4.1.2 |
From the absence of a cause, the absence of an effect [follows]. | KVs 4.1.3 |
'Non-eternal' — this is a specific negation of [its] existence. | KVs 4.1.4 |
[This is due to] ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). | KVs 4.1.5 |
Perception [of earth] is due to its being large, possessing many substances, and having color (<s>rūpa</s>). | KVs 4.1.6 |
Although air (<s>vāyu</s>) possesses substantiality and largeness, it is not perceived because of the absence of color and [perceptible] impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>). | KVs 4.1.7 |
The perception of color is due to inherence in many substances and due to the specificity of color. | KVs 4.1.8 |
By this, the cognition of taste, smell, and touch has been explained. | KVs 4.1.9 |
From the absence of that [i.e., color], there is no deviation [of the rule]. | KVs 4.1.10 |

children.text: saṃkhyāḥ parimāṇāni pṛthaktvaṃ saṃyoga vibhāgau paratvāparatve karma ca rūpadravyasamavāyāt cākṣuṣāṇi | KVs_4,1.11 |
children.translated_text: Numbers, measures, separateness, conjunction, disjunction, remoteness, proximity, and motion — because of their co-inherence with color-possessing substance, [these] are visual [i.e., perceivable by the eye]. | KVs 4.1.11 |
In colorless [substances], they are non-visual. | KVs 4.1.12 |

children.text: etena guṇatve bhāve ca sarvendriyaṃ jñānaṃ vyākhyātam | KVs_4,1.13 |
children.translated_text: By this, the cognition [that is common to] all sense-faculties regarding qualities and existence has been explained. | KVs 4.1.13 |
Moreover, the effect-substances of earth and so forth are of three kinds, designated as body, sense-faculty, and object. | KVs 4.2.1 |

children.text: pratyakṣāpratyakṣāṇāṃ saṃyogasyāpratyakṣatvāt pañcātmakaṃ na vidyate | KVs_4,2.2 |
children.translated_text: Since the conjunction of the perceptible and the imperceptible is imperceptible, a five-element [body] does not exist. | KVs 4.2.2 |
And because of the non-appearance of a further quality, a three-element [body] does not exist. | KVs 4.2.3 |
But the conjunction of atoms is not [thereby] precluded. | KVs 4.2.4 |

children.text: tatra śarīraṃ dvividhaṃ yonijamayonijaṃ ca | KVs_4,2.5 |
children.translated_text: There, the body is of two kinds: born from a womb (<s>yonija</s>) and not born from a womb (<s>ayonija</s>). | KVs 4.2.5 |
Because it is not preceded by a fixed direction and place. | KVs 4.2.6 |
And because of a special <s>dharma</s> (merit). | KVs 4.2.7 |
And because of the absence of a [common] designation. | KVs 4.2.8 |
Because naming is [something] initial [i.e., given at the beginning of creation]. | KVs 4.2.9 |
There are [bodies] not born from a womb. | KVs 4.2.10 |
And from the evidence of the <s>Veda</s>. | KVs 4.2.11 |
Through the conjunction of the self and through effort, there is motion (<s>karma</s>) in the hand. | KVs 5.1.1 |
Likewise, through conjunction with the hand, there is motion in the pestle. | KVs 5.1.2 |

children.text: abhighātaje musalādau karmaṇi vyatirekādakāraṇaṃ hastasaṃyogaḥ | KVs_5,1.3 |
children.translated_text: In the motion produced by impact (<s>abhighāta</s>) in the pestle and so forth, the conjunction with the hand is not the cause, due to its separateness [from that motion]. | KVs 5.1.3 |
Likewise, the conjunction with the self [is not the cause] in the motion of the hand [produced by impact]. | KVs 5.1.4 |
Through impact, from the conjunction with the pestle, there is motion in the hand. | KVs 5.1.5 |
And from the conjunction with the self, there is motion [back] to the self. | KVs 5.1.6 |
In the absence of conjunction, falling [occurs] due to gravity (<s>gurutva</s>). | KVs 5.1.7 |
Due to the absence of a special impulsion (<s>nodana</s>), there is neither upward nor sideways movement. | KVs 5.1.8 |
From a special effort, there is a special impulsion. | KVs 5.1.9 |
From a special impulsion, there is a special throwing upward. | KVs 5.1.10 |
By the motion of the hand, the motion of a ball has been explained. | KVs 5.1.11 |
Likewise, in the bursting of what has been burned. | KVs 5.1.12 |
The movement of one asleep, in the absence of effort [is due to unseen causes]. | KVs 5.1.13 |
The motion in grass is from the conjunction with air. | KVs 5.1.14 |
The movement of a magnet [toward iron] and the movement of a needle [toward a lodestone] are caused by the unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>). | KVs 5.1.15 |
In an arrow, the non-simultaneous conjunctions of different [parts] are the reason for [its being a case of] different motions. | KVs 5.1.16 |

children.text: nodanādādyamiṣoḥ karma tatkarmakāritācca saṃskārāduttaraṃ tathottaramuttaraṃ ca | KVs_5,1.17 |
children.translated_text: Through impulsion, the initial motion of the arrow; and from that motion, a <s>saṃskāra</s> (residual impression) produced; from that <s>saṃskāra</s>, a subsequent [motion]; and likewise, a further subsequent [motion]. | KVs 5.1.17 |
In the absence of <s>saṃskāra</s>, falling [occurs] due to gravity. | KVs 5.1.18 |
Through impulsion, impact, conjunction-with-the-conjoined, there is motion in earth. | KVs 5.2.1 |
The specific [varieties of that motion] are caused by the unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>). | KVs 5.2.2 |
In the absence of conjunction, water falls due to gravity. | KVs 5.2.3 |
Due to fluidity (<s>dravatva</s>), [there is] flowing. | KVs 5.2.4 |
The ascending of [water] in a tube is from conjunction with air. | KVs 5.2.5 |
And from impulsion, pressing, and conjunction-with-the-conjoined. | KVs 5.2.6 |
The creeping of [sap] toward a tree — this is caused by the unseen. | KVs 5.2.7 |

children.text: apāṃ saṅghāto vilayanaṃ ca tejaḥ saṃyogāt | KVs_5,2.8 |
children.translated_text: The solidification and liquefaction of water is from conjunction with fire. | KVs 5.2.8 |
Lightning is the mark of that [conjunction of fire and water]. | KVs 5.2.9 |
And [this is known] from the <s>Veda</s>. | KVs 5.2.10 |
Thunder is from the conjunction and disjunction of water [and fire]. | KVs 5.2.11 |

children.text: pṛthivīkarmaṇā tejaḥ karma vāyukarma ca vyākhyātam | KVs_5,2.12 |
children.translated_text: By the motion of earth, the motion of fire and the motion of air have been explained. | KVs 5.2.12 |

children.text: agnerūrdhvajvalanaṃ vāyostiryaggamanaṃ aṇūnāṃ manasaścādyaṃ karmādṛṣṭakāritam | KVs_5,2.13 |
children.translated_text: The upward blazing of fire, the sideways movement of air, the initial motion of atoms, and [the initial motion] of mind — [all these are] caused by the unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>). | KVs 5.2.13 |
By the motion of the hand, the motion of the mind has been explained. | KVs 5.2.14 |
From the contact of self, sense-faculty, mind, and object, [there arise] pleasure and pain. | KVs 5.2.15 |

children.text: tadanārambha ātmasthe manasi śarīrasya duḥkhābhāvaḥ saṃyogaḥ | KVs_5,2.16 |
children.translated_text: In the non-initiation of that [contact], when the mind is fixed in the self, the absence of suffering for the body is [the state of] <s>yoga</s> (conjunction/union). | KVs 5.2.16 |
Moving away, moving toward, [bodily processes such as] conjunction with what is eaten and drunk, conjunctions with other effects — these are caused by the unseen. | KVs 5.2.17 |
In the absence of that [unseen], the absence of conjunction, the non-appearance [of further effects] — that is <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). | KVs 5.2.18 |
Darkness is the absence [of light], due to the dissimilarity with the production of substance, quality, and motion. | KVs 5.2.19 |
And because of the obstruction of fire by another substance. | KVs 5.2.20 |
Direction (<s>dik</s>), time (<s>kāla</s>), and space (<s>ākāśa</s>) are without motion, due to their dissimilarity with [substances] that possess motion. | KVs 5.2.21 |
By this, motions and qualities have been explained. | KVs 5.2.22 |
For those without motion, inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) of motions is precluded. | KVs 5.2.23 |
But the cause [for direction and time] is qualities that do not co-inhere [with motions]. | KVs 5.2.24 |
Direction has been explained through qualities. | KVs 5.2.25 |
Time [has been explained] through [its] cause. | KVs 5.2.26 |
In the <s>Veda</s>, the composition of sentences is preceded by intelligence (<s>buddhi</s>). | KVs 6.1.1 |
The accomplishment of naming-action among <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> is the inferential mark [of an intelligent author of the Veda]. | KVs 6.1.2 |
The act of giving is preceded by intelligence. | KVs 6.1.3 |
Likewise, receiving. | KVs 6.1.4 |
Because the qualities of one self are not the cause [of qualities] in another self. | KVs 6.1.5 |
That [merit] does not exist in [the case of accepting] food [offered by one who is] corrupt. | KVs 6.1.6 |
'Corrupt' [means] in connection with injury (<s>hiṃsā</s>). | KVs 6.1.7 |
Of that [food], the fault is from its being uttered in conjunction [with the corrupt donor]. | KVs 6.1.8 |
That [fault] does not exist in [food from one who is] not corrupt. | KVs 6.1.9 |
Activity [should be directed] toward one who is superior. | KVs 6.1.10 |
Activity [may be directed] toward one who is equal or inferior. | KVs 6.1.11 |

children.text: etena hīnasamaviśiṣṭa dhārmikebhyaḥ parasvādānaṃ vyākhyātam | KVs_6,1.12 |
children.translated_text: By this, the taking of another's property from those who are inferior, equal, or superior in <s>dharma</s> has been explained. | KVs 6.1.12 |
Likewise, the abandonment of adversaries. | KVs 6.1.13 |
When the other [party] is inferior, [there should be] abandonment [of the dispute]. | KVs 6.1.14 |
When equal, [there may be] self-sacrifice or sacrifice of the other. | KVs 6.1.15 |
When [the other is] superior, self-sacrifice. | KVs 6.1.16 |
Of actions having both visible and invisible purposes, in the absence of a visible [purpose], the purpose is for <s>abhyudaya</s> (worldly prosperity). KVs 6.2.1

Ritual bathing (<s>abhiṣecana</s>), fasting (<s>upavāsa</s>), celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), dwelling in the teacher's house (<s>gurukulavāsa</s>), the forest-hermit life (<s>vānaprastha</s>), sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>), gifts (<s>dāna</s>), sprinkling (<s>prokṣaṇa</s>), observance of directions, asterisms, mantras, and time-rules — [these are] for the invisible [purpose] (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>). KVs 6.2.2
The four stages of life (<s>cāturāśramya</s>), [observances] with qualification (<s>upadhā</s>) and without qualification (<s>anupadhā</s>). KVs 6.2.3
The fault of [mere] existence is a qualified fault; the unqualified [observance is faultless]. KVs 6.2.4
That which, having the desired color, taste, smell, and touch, is sprinkled and ritually bathed — that is pure (<s>śuci</s>). KVs 6.2.5
'Impure' (<s>aśuci</s>) is the negation of 'pure.' KVs 6.2.6
And [it is] a distinct category. KVs 6.2.7

children.text: ayatasya śucibhojanādabhyudayo na vidyate niyamābhāvād vidyate vār'thāntaratvād yamasya | KVs_6,2.8 |
children.translated_text: For one who is undisciplined, there is no <s>abhyudaya</s> (worldly prosperity) from eating pure food, due to the absence of rules; or there is, since discipline (<s>yama</s>) is a distinct category. KVs 6.2.8
And in its absence, [there is no prosperity] because of non-existence. KVs 6.2.9
From pleasure [arises] attachment (<s>rāga</s>). KVs 6.2.10
And because of being absorbed in that [pleasure]. KVs 6.2.11
And from <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (the unseen). KVs 6.2.12
And from a particular birth (<s>jātiviśeṣa</s>). KVs 6.2.13
Activity toward <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit) is preceded by desire (<s>icchā</s>) and aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>). KVs 6.2.14
The conjunction and disjunction of that [activity with its causes]. KVs 6.2.15
<s>Mokṣa</s> (liberation) has been explained [in the discussion] of the actions of the self (<s>ātmakarma</s>). KVs 6.2.16
Qualities have been stated. KVs 7.1.1
The color, taste, smell, and touch of earth and the like are non-eternal, because the substance is non-eternal. KVs 7.1.2
By this, the eternality [of these qualities] in eternal [substances] is stated. KVs 7.1.3

children.text: apsu tejasi vāyau ca nityā dravyanityavāt | KVs_7,1.4 |
children.translated_text: In water, fire, and air, [qualities are] eternal, because the substance is eternal. KVs 7.1.4
In non-eternal [substances], [qualities are] non-eternal, because the substance is non-eternal. KVs 7.1.5
In earth, those [qualities] produced by heat (<s>pākaja</s>) are preceded by the qualities of the cause. KVs 7.1.6
Because of being [inhering] in one substance. KVs 7.1.7
The perception and non-perception of the atomic and the great in eternal [substances] has been explained. KVs 7.1.8
And because of the multiplicity of causes. KVs 7.1.9
The opposite of that is the atom (<s>aṇu</s>). KVs 7.1.10

children.text: aṇu mahaditi tasmin viśeṣabhāvāt viśeṣābhāvācca | KVs_7,1.11 |
children.translated_text: 'Atomic' and 'great' — because of the presence of a specific [quality] in that, and because of the absence of a specific [quality]. KVs 7.1.11
Because of simultaneity. KVs 7.1.12
And from the example. KVs 7.1.13
The absence of atomic-ness and great-ness in atomic-ness and great-ness has been explained through actions and qualities. KVs 7.1.14

children.text: karmabhiḥ karmāṇi guṇaiśca guṇā vyākhyātāḥ | KVs_7,1.15 |
children.translated_text: Actions [are explained] by actions, and qualities by qualities. KVs 7.1.15
And actions and qualities are explained by atomic-ness and great-ness. KVs 7.1.16
By this, length (<s>dīrghatva</s>) and shortness (<s>hrasvatva</s>) are explained. KVs 7.1.17
In a non-eternal [substance], [dimension is] non-eternal. KVs 7.1.18
In an eternal [substance], [dimension is] eternal. KVs 7.1.19
The spherical (<s>parimaṇḍala</s>) [dimension of the atom] is eternal. KVs 7.1.20
And ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is the mark of knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>). KVs 7.1.21
Because of all-pervasiveness, space (<s>ākāśa</s>) is great; and likewise the self (<s>ātman</s>). KVs 7.1.22
Because of the absence of that [all-pervasiveness], the mind (<s>manas</s>) is atomic. KVs 7.1.23
Direction (<s>dik</s>) is explained through qualities. KVs 7.1.24
Time (<s>kāla</s>) [is explained] through the cause. KVs 7.1.25
Distinct from color, taste, smell, and touch — oneness (<s>ekatva</s>) is a separate category. KVs 7.2.1
Likewise, separateness (<s>pṛthaktva</s>). KVs 7.2.2
The absence of single-oneness and single-separateness in oneness and separateness has been explained by [analogy with] atomic-ness and great-ness. KVs 7.2.3

children.text: niḥ saṃkhyatvāt karmaguṇānāṃ sarvaikatvaṃ na vidyate | KVs_7,2.4 |
children.translated_text: Because of the innumerability of actions and qualities, universal oneness does not exist. KVs 7.2.4
That [view of universal oneness] is erroneous. KVs 7.2.5
Because of the absence of oneness, division [into parts] does not exist. KVs 7.2.6
Because of the absence of single-oneness and single-separateness in the cause and effect [pair], oneness and separateness [of cause and effect] do not exist. KVs 7.2.7
This has been explained for non-eternal [entities]. KVs 7.2.8
Conjunction [arises] from the action of one, from the action of both, and from [prior] conjunction. KVs 7.2.9
By this, disjunction (<s>vibhāga</s>) is explained. KVs 7.2.10
The absence of conjunction and disjunction in conjunction and disjunction has been explained by [analogy with] atomic-ness and great-ness. KVs 7.2.11

children.text: karmabhiḥ karmāṇi guṇairguṇā aṇutva mahattvābhyāmiti | KVs_7,2.12 |
children.translated_text: Actions by actions, qualities by qualities, and by atomic-ness and great-ness — thus. KVs 7.2.12

children.text: yutasiddhyabhāvāt kāryakāraṇayoḥ saṃyogavibhāgau na vidyete | KVs_7,2.13 |
children.translated_text: Because of the absence of separate existence (<s>yutasiddhi</s>), conjunction and disjunction do not exist in the cause-and-effect [relation]. KVs 7.2.13
Because of being a quality. KVs 7.2.14
A quality too is conceived. KVs 7.2.15
Because of being actionless. KVs 7.2.16
And because of the usage 'In the absence [of something], [it] does not exist.' KVs 7.2.17
Word and meaning are not [intrinsically] connected. KVs 7.2.18
[This follows] from [the distinction between] the stick conjoined [with the substance] and the particular inherent [in the substance]. KVs 7.2.19
The cognition of meaning from a word is conventional (<s>sāmayika</s>). KVs 7.2.20
'Farther' and 'nearer' [arise] from two things in one direction, from two things at one time, from one that is proximate and one that is remote. KVs 7.2.21
And because of the farther-ness of the cause, and the nearer-ness of the cause. KVs 7.2.22
The absence of farther-ness and nearer-ness in farther-ness and nearer-ness has been explained by [analogy with] atomic-ness and great-ness. KVs 7.2.23
Actions by actions. KVs 7.2.24
Qualities by qualities. KVs 7.2.25

children.text: ihedamiti yataḥ kāryakāraṇayoḥ sa samavāyaḥ | KVs_7,2.26 |
children.translated_text: 'This [inheres] in that' — from which [relation] the cause and effect [are so related], that is <s>samavāya</s> (inherence). KVs 7.2.26
By virtue of its being the reality [of the relation]. KVs 7.2.27
Knowledge in substances has been explained. KVs 8.1.1
Therein, the self (<s>ātman</s>) and the mind (<s>manas</s>) are imperceptible. KVs 8.1.2
In the exposition of knowledge, the method of the production of knowledge has been stated. KVs 8.1.3

children.text: guṇakarmasu sannikṛṣṭeṣu jñānaniṣpatteḥ dravyaṃ kāraṇam | KVs_8,1.4 |
children.translated_text: When qualities and actions are in contact [with the senses], substance is the cause of the production of knowledge. KVs 8.1.4
In universals and particulars, because of the absence of [further] universals and particulars, that [knowledge] is just knowledge. KVs 8.1.5
[Knowledge] depends on universals and particulars in substances, qualities, and actions. KVs 8.1.6
In substance, [knowledge] depends on substance, quality, and action. KVs 8.1.7

children.text: guṇakarmasu guṇakarmābhāvāt guṇakarmāpekṣaṃ na vidyate | KVs_8,1.8 |
children.translated_text: In qualities and actions, because of the absence of [further] qualities and actions, dependence on qualities and actions does not exist. KVs 8.1.8

children.text: samavāyinaḥ śvaityācchvaitya buddheśca śvete budviste ete kāryakāraṇabhūte | KVs_8,1.9 |
children.translated_text: From the whiteness of an inherent [substance], the cognition of whiteness; and in what is white, the cognition — these two stand in the relation of cause and effect. KVs 8.1.9
In substances, [cognitions] are not mutually caused. KVs 8.1.10

children.text: kāraṇāyaugapadyāt kāraṇakramācca ghaṭapaṭādibuddhīnāṃ kramo na hetuphalabhāvāt | KVs_8,1.11 |
children.translated_text: Because of the non-simultaneity of causes and because of the sequence of causes, the sequence of cognitions of pot, cloth, and the like is not due to the relation of cause and effect. KVs 8.1.11

children.text: ayameṣa tvayā kṛtaṃ bhojayainaṃ iti buddhyapekṣam | KVs_8,2.1 |
children.translated_text: 'This is he,' 'done by you,' 'feed him' — [these] depend on cognition. KVs 8.2.1
Because of existence in what is perceived, and absence in what is not perceived. KVs 8.2.2
'Object' (<s>artha</s>) [is used] with reference to substances, qualities, and actions. KVs 8.2.3
The five-element nature of substances has been denied. KVs 8.2.4

children.text: bhūyastvāt gandhavattvācca pṛthivī gandhajñāne prakṛtiḥ | KVs_8,2.5 |
children.translated_text: Because of predominance and because of possessing smell, earth is the basis in the cognition of smell. KVs 8.2.5
Likewise water, fire, and air, with respect to taste, color, and touch [respectively], due to the non-specificity [of those qualities in the others]. KVs 8.2.6
Prior to [its production, the effect] is non-existent, because of the absence of designation of action and quality. KVs 9.1.1
[It is] existent and non-existent. KVs 9.1.2
Because of the absence of designation of action and quality in the non-existent, [it is] a distinct category. KVs 9.1.3
[What is] existent and non-existent. KVs 9.1.4
And that which is other than the non-existent, from that [it follows that it is] non-existent. KVs 9.1.5
'[It is] non-existent' — because of the absence of perception of [something] that has come into being, [and] like the perception opposed to the memory of [something] that has been. KVs 9.1.6
And because of the perception of existence in the state of such absence. KVs 9.1.7
By this, 'non-pot,' 'non-cow,' and '<s>adharma</s>' (demerit) are explained. KVs 9.1.8
'What has not come into being does not exist' — this is not a separate meaning. KVs 9.1.9

children.text: nāsti ghaṭo gehe iti sato ghaṭasya gehasaṃsargapratiṣedhaḥ | KVs_9,1.10 |
children.translated_text: 'There is no pot in the house' — this is the negation of the connection of the [existing] pot with the house. KVs 9.1.10
In the self, from the conjunction of the self and the mind, [arises] perception of the self. KVs 9.1.11
Likewise, perception in other substances. KVs 9.1.12
For those whose inner instrument is unsteady, and for those who have withdrawn from <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) — and of those [perceptions]. KVs 9.1.13
From inherence in that [self], [arises knowledge] of actions and qualities [of the self]. KVs 9.1.14
From inherence in the self, [arises knowledge] of the qualities of the self. KVs 9.1.15

children.text: asyedaṃ kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ saṃyogi virodhi samavāyi ceti laiṅgikam | KVs_9,2.1 |
children.translated_text: 'This is the effect of that,' 'this is the cause of that,' 'this is conjoined with that,' 'this is opposed to that,' 'this inheres in that' — [these are] inferential (<s>laiṅgika</s>). KVs 9.2.1
'This is the effect of that' — the cause-effect relation arises from the parts. KVs 9.2.2
By this, verbal testimony (<s>śābda</s>) is explained. KVs 9.2.3
Reason (<s>hetu</s>), designation (<s>apadeśa</s>), mark (<s>liṅga</s>), means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), and instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) — [these are] not different [in meaning]. KVs 9.2.4
'This belongs to that' — because it depends on cognition. KVs 9.2.5
Memory (<s>smṛti</s>) [arises] from a particular conjunction of the self [with the mind] and from [mental] impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>). KVs 9.2.6
Likewise, dream (<s>svapna</s>). KVs 9.2.7
[Dream is close to] waking. KVs 9.2.8
And from <s>dharma</s> (merit). KVs 9.2.9
From a defect of the sense organ and from a defect of impression [arises] <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance/error). KVs 9.2.10
That is defective knowledge. KVs 9.2.11
Non-defective [knowledge] is <s>vidyā</s> (valid knowledge). KVs 9.2.12
The [knowledge of] sages (<s>ārṣa</s>) and the vision of perfected beings (<s>siddhadarśana</s>) [arise] from <s>dharma</s> (merit). KVs 9.2.13
Because of the specific causation of the desired and the undesired, and because of mutual opposition, pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) and pain (<s>duḥkha</s>) are distinct categories. KVs 10.1.1
And the lack of an intermediate [state] between doubt and certainty is a reason for [their] being different kinds of knowledge. KVs 10.1.2
The production of those two [pleasure and pain] is from perception and inference. KVs 10.1.3
'It was' — also [thus]. KVs 10.1.4
And from the non-observation of the effect even when [the cause] exists. KVs 10.1.5
Because [pleasure and pain] are observed in other causes co-inhering in one object. KVs 10.1.6

children.text: ekadeśe ityekasmin śiraḥ pṛṣṭhamudaraṃ marmāṇi tadviśeṣastadviśeṣebhyaḥ | KVs_10,1.7 |
children.translated_text: 'In one part' — in one [body], head, back, abdomen, vital points — that specificity, from those specificities. KVs 10.1.7
'It is a cause' — because the effect inheres in the substance. KVs 10.2.1
Or from conjunction. KVs 10.2.2
From inherence in the cause, actions [arise]. KVs 10.2.3
Likewise, regarding <s>rūpa</s> (color/form), because of <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) in a single object that is the cause. KVs 10.2.4.
The <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction) of a cloth [with its color] is due to <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) in the cause. KVs 10.2.5.
And [also] because of <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) in what is both cause and non-cause. KVs 10.2.6.
The distinctive [color] of fire is due to <s>saṃyuktasamavāya</s> (inherence in what is conjoined). KVs 10.2.7.
The application of things that are seen and whose purposes are seen, in the absence of what is seen, is for the sake of <s>abhyudaya</s> (prosperity/spiritual elevation). KVs 10.2.8.
From the statement of that [principle], the authoritativeness of the <s>Āmnāya</s> (Vedic tradition) [is established] — thus. KVs 10.2.9.
